parent_verification.text: The GFC precedent is instructive but not perfectly analogous. When Miami's condo market collapsed, **22,000 units sat unsold** and inventory reached **52 months of supply**. Building-level data reveals staggering non-closing rates: Onyx on the Bay saw only **45% of units close**; Wind by Neo managed roughly **11%**; Icon Brickell was **4.9% occupied** by 2009. Downtown prices fell **41.8%**. Today's 23-month inventory is alarming but not yet catastrophic. The buyer profile has shifted decisively — **78–83% of transactions above $2,000/SF are all-cash**, versus the speculative flippers who dominated pre-2008 sales. OZK management's claim that 11 of 14 Miami condo loans have presales covering full loan repayment provides meaningful but unverifiable comfort.
